entries.title: White Sox polled on team's top first-half players, moments — and how far they'll go from here
entries.summary: <p>Before he got hurt May 29, there was zero question who was putting the “M” in MVP of the surprisingly competitive <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" >White Sox</a>: Japanese rookie <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/07/10/white-sox-activate-munetaka-murakami-from-injured-list-option-jacob-gonzalez-to-charlotte" target="_blank" >Munetaka Murakami</a>, only the third Sox player to slug 20 home runs pre-June, joining Frank Thomas (1994) and Jim Thome (2006).</p><p>Since then, the Sox have had several pairs of hands on the wheel, steering them into a first-place tie with the Guardians in the American League Central entering their final series before the All-Star break.</p><p>So, who is the team’s first-half MVP? Is it 20-homer <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/07/04/miguel-vargas-chicago-white-sox-all-star-game-third-baseman-joe-crede-colson-montgomery-davis-martin" target="_blank" >infielder Miguel Vargas</a>, who will represent the team at the All-Star Game in Philadelphia? Infielder Colson Montgomery, with his 23 bombs? Starting pitcher Davis Martin, who has held things down with nine wins and a team-high 3.0 WAR? Someone else?</p><p>The Sun-Times poked around Rate Field asking for top threes.</p><p>Center fielder Tristan Peters and pitchers Grant Taylor and Erik Fedde each had Vargas and Martin 1-2. But Peters went with Taylor third, Taylor with rookie left fielder Sam Antonacci and Fedde with Peters.</p><p>“Sam is my sleeper pick,” Taylor said. “He brings something different to the clubhouse.”</p><p>“We weren’t sure what we were going to get in center this year, and [Peters] has been an unbelievable asset,” Fedde said.</p><p>Infielder Chase Meidroth’s top three: Montgomery, Murakami and Vargas. Pitcher Noah Schultz’s: Martin, Montgomery and Vargas.</p><p>Injured pitcher Mike Vasil, the cheerleader-in-chief, had it Murakami, Vargas and Antonacci, whom he called a “complete motor in this lineup.”</p><p>Said longtime TV analyst Steve Stone, “It’s Davis Martin, Vargas and you probably go, because of the power numbers, with Colson Montgomery. However, honorable mention certainly goes to Sam Antonacci.”</p><p><b>THE first-half moment</b></p><p>We also asked which play, win or other occurrence belongs at the top of this team’s list so far.</p><p>Meidroth kept to a broad stroke — “just giving ourselves a chance in the second half” — while Taylor pointed to the Sox’ seven walk-off wins.</p><p>“It sets the standard for what we’re doing because we’re never out of a game,” Taylor said. “We always have the chance to fight back. Bottom nine, we’re coming to play.”</p><p>One of those walk-offs came on Braden Montgomery’s two-run homer in the 10th inning to beat the Braves 6-5 at Rate Field on June 9 in the outfielder’s very first big-league game.</p><p>“That was the play for me,” Schultz said. “A guy gets called up and makes an immediate impact like that? Such a huge deal and really brought the team together.”</p><p>Peters and Fedde opted for the series win against the Cubs in mid-May. It ended with another two-run, 10th-inning blast, this one off the bat of catcher Edgar Quero to take the rubber match 9-8 in a wild scene on the South Side.</p><p>“I think that was one of the first times we all had belief that we were coming together well and playing good baseball,” Fedde said. “The whole hype of the city came out, and winning that series kind of cemented the thought that we were going to compete.”</p><p>Vasil threw a bit of a curveball, impressive for a guy recovering from Tommy John surgery.</p><p>“The easy one to say is the Quero walk-off against the Cubs, but I honestly think the biggest swing that took us in the right direction was the [Andrew] Benintendi home run [in the ninth inning on April 23] in Arizona. A three-run bomb in a tie game on the road? That was when it sort of turned for us for the year.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">EDGAR QUERO WALK-OFF HOME RUN THE WHITE SOX TAKE A SERIES FROM THE CUBS <a href="https://t.co/JPTSqeOHdP">pic.twitter.com/JPTSqeOHdP</a></p>— Talkin' Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) <a href="https://x.com/TalkinBaseball_/status/2056125478595891627?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">May 17, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p><b>What happens from here?</b></p><p>When Murakami finally re-entered the lineup Friday, his hamstring trouble hopefully behind him, it felt almost like a major trade-deadline acquisition. Of course, it wasn’t one, and general manager Chris Getz soon will be on the clock to show how willing the Sox are to improve their roster from outside the organization.</p><p>Stone — who predicted on Opening Day the Sox would be much better than the 66 or 67 wins most analytics models projected for them — isn’t offering a second-half forecast this far out from the August 3 deadline.</p><p>“I don’t think there is any way Chris Getz wants to break up a farm system that he worked so hard to put together,” Stone said, “but it’s probably no secret they could use a starting pitcher [and] maybe another arm for the bullpen.”</p><p>The Guardians, Twins and Tigers all could be in play for the division title. A wild-card spot could be there for the grabbing in an AL with only two teams — the Rays and the Yankees — well clear of .500.</p><p>How are Sox players sizing up their chances?</p><p>“I easily see the talent of this team going into the playoffs,” Meidroth said. “At this point, it’s up to us.”</p><p>“We can win our division,” Peters said. “There’s no doubt in my mind.”</p><p>According to Fedde, anything less than a division title would be a “disappointment.” Sox fans who have witnessed three straight 100-plus-loss seasons might be more inclined to welcome any old postseason berth.</p><p>A couple of pitchers stuck their necks out even further.</p><p>“With Mune back, I think we’re going to play similar or better ball as we go forward, continue to build on what we’ve gone and grow and get better, and then we want to be playing deep into October,” Taylor said. “That’s the goals I have and what I expect from this team.”</p><p>Schultz put it all the way out there.</p><p>“Win the division, host playoff games, win the World Series,” he said. “If you’re not shooting for that, then you’re not playing the right sport.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/07/10/white-sox-activate-munetaka-murakami-from-injured-list-option-jacob-gonzalez-to-charlotte" >White Sox activate Munetaka Murakami from injured list, option Jacob Gonzalez to Charlotte</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/07/04/miguel-vargas-chicago-white-sox-all-star-game-third-baseman-joe-crede-colson-montgomery-davis-martin" target="_blank" >Miguel Vargas becomes White Sox’ first All-Star third baseman since Joe Crede in 2008</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Court monitor dings city for lacking a single compliant accessible crosswalk signal for impaired pedestrians
entries.summary: <p>One year after a federal judge ordered Chicago to install more accessible crosswalk signals for impaired pedestrians, a court-appointed monitor found the city has met the minimum requirements by installing 78 new signals.</p><p>But the monitor, in its <a class="Link" href="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/d3/e7/21bd91c14354aaf73233c7276cd6/pedestrian-crossing-monitor-report.pdf" target="_blank" >first-year report</a> published July 1, also found that none of Chicago's accessible signals — with their distinctive audible beeping — are compliant with federal standards.</p><p>"They're usable. But they're not as effective as they can and should be," says Rachel M. Weisberg, directing attorney at Disability Rights Advocates, which filed the original lawsuit in 2019 that led to court-appointed monitor Michael G. Shaw being named in June 2025.</p><p>The signals, when pressed, beep when it's safe to cross for blind and vision-impaired pedestrians. The buttons also vibrate to alert hearing-impaired pedestrians of a signal change.</p><p>The standards for the crosswalks, called accessible pedestrian signals, are determined by the U.S. Department of Transportation's Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices. The manual sets the technical specifications from everything from the height of button placement to the signal's distance from the curb, Weisberg said.</p><p>Besides failing the technical requirements, the monitor found that many devices were not functioning properly or required maintenance.</p><p>The city has work to do on that end, Weisberg said. But the city has made substantial progress at identifying and constructing accessible signals at crosswalks across the city.</p><p>In the first year under court supervision, the monitor found:<br></p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-5310e822-7c79-11f1-9253-cbff6d5e8685"><li>The city installed 78 accessible pedestrian signals, eight more than what the court required. The requirements ramp up in the coming years. The city is required to build signals at 110 intersections in the second year of the judge's remedial order.</li><li>The city now has accessible signals at 165 intersections — only 6.5% of the city's 2,800 total intersections.</li><li>The Chicago Department of Transportation "demonstrated exemplary efforts" in following the judge's order, and has drafted an accessible pedestrian signal policy and has built several accessible signals at intersections requested by the public.</li></ul><p>The spokesperson for the Transportation Department, which oversees the installation of accessible signals, did not immediately have a comment on the monitor's report, but pointed to a June <a class="Link" href="https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/cdot/provdrs/traffic_signals_andstreetlights/news/2026/june/city-of-chicago-expands-accessible-pedestrian-signals-citywide--.html" target="_blank" >news release</a> about the new accessible signals.</p><p>Since 2019, the city has built accessible signals at all intersection reconstruction projects, the release states. </p><p>"This significant expansion of Accessible Pedestrian Signals is about making our streets more inclusive and ensuring residents who are blind or have low vision can travel more independently in every neighborhood," Mayor Brandon Johnson was quoted as saying in the release. His office did not immediately reply to a request for comment.</p><p>The city has website, <a class="Link" href="https://www.chicagoaps.org/" target="_blank" >chicagoaps.org/</a>, with a map of Chicago's accessible intersections. The site also has a form for residents to request new accessible signals.</p><p>U.S. District Judge LaShona Hunt <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2025/03/19/blind-visually-impaired-pedestrian-crossing-intersections-judge-order-installation" target="_blank" >placed the city under a remedial order</a> in March 2025, aiming to resolve a lawsuit filed six years ago by the American Council of the Blind of Metropolitan Chicago.</p><p>The lawsuit accused the city of violating the Americans for Disabilities Act by failing to build signalized street intersections with accessible pedestrian signals.</p><p>The order mandates the city to install the devices at at least 71% of signaled intersections by the end of 2035, and five additional years to hit the 100% mark.</p><p>For years, Chicago officials talked about launching pilot programs to address the scarcity of accessible signals, Weisberg said. She's heartened to see the city finally taking the issue seriously.</p><p>Other cities have been slow to adopt accessible signals. New York City lost a lawsuit in 2022 that claimed it violated the Americans for Disabilities Act because it lacked accessible signals at 95% of its intersections. That city is now under a similar court order.</p><p>Disability Rights Advocates <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2025/09/10/chicago-pedestrian-ways-violate-ada-requirements-lawsuit-alleges" target="_blank" >filed another lawsuit</a> last year alleging the city has not done enough to improve the accessibility of its sidewalks and curbs.</p><p>With time, Chicago could become a model for accessible infrastructure, Weisberg said.</p><p>"The hope is that Chicago can be a leader to support the blind and vision-impaired community," she said.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe src="https://docs.google.com/viewer?embedded=true&url=https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/d3/e7/21bd91c14354aaf73233c7276cd6/pedestrian-crossing-monitor-report.pdf"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p></p>

entries.title: 2 killed in minivan-semitruck crash in Hegewisch
entries.summary: <p>Two people inside a minivan died when they rear-ended a semitruck Friday morning in the Far South Side's Hegewisch neighborhood, police said.</p><p>The semi was eastbound in the 2700 block of East 130th Street about 9:15 a.m., trying to make a left turn when a Dodge Grand Caravan, also eastbound, rear-ended the semi, police said. </p><p>The two people in the minivan, identified only as male, were taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center where they were pronounced dead, police said. </p><p>No one else was hurt. </p><p>The police major accidents investigation unit is probing the wreck. <br></p>

entries.title: Los arrestos de ICE han aumentado en Chicago, pero con tácticas menos llamativas que el otoño pasado
entries.summary: <p>La aplicación federal de la ley de inmigración se ha intensificado en Chicago en las últimas semanas, pero las tácticas de la administración de Trump han sido mucho menos publicitadas que durante el auge de su campaña de deportación el otoño pasado, dicen grupos legales y defensores de la inmigración.</p><p>La semana pasada, al menos 20 personas fueron arrestadas por el Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas (ICE) en Chicago, y otras 17 personas han sido detenidas esta semana hasta ahora, según informes de grupos de respuesta rápida que documentan los arrestos.</p><p>Esos números parecen ser un aumento con respecto a los meses recientes, dijo Marcela Rodríguez, copresidenta de la Agenda Latina de Illinois y miembro del grupo sin fines de lucro Enlace Chicago.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-c30000" name="module-c30000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>El lado suroeste, particularmente los vecindarios de Back of the Yards, Brighton Park y Gage Park, han sido los más afectados recientemente, dijeron los grupos legales.</p><p>La actividad aumentada de ICE en Chicago ocurre en medio de una campaña de deportación escalada por la administración de Trump en todo el país.</p><p>El martes, un oficial de ICE le disparó y mató a un hombre en Houston durante un intento de detención de tráfico.</p><p>Durante el período de cinco días a finales de junio, ICE arrestó a más de 10,000 personas. Las cifras indican que, aunque la administración ya no se concentra en esfuerzos llamativos en ciudades individuales, los arrestos continúan y están en aumento.</p><p>“Estos números representan más que estadísticas”, dijo Rodríguez el jueves en una conferencia de prensa en Back of the Yards con numerosos líderes de defensa de inmigrantes. “Representan a padres, hijos, trabajadores, vecinos, propietarios de negocios pequeños y miembros de nuestra comunidad que merecen dignidad, justicia y debido proceso”.</p><p>Los grupos legales dijeron que esos números también pueden subestimar la cantidad real de arrestos porque los agentes federales de inmigración han operado de manera más discreta en comparación con el otoño pasado, cuando caravanas de agentes vestidos con uniformes militares recorrían las calles, utilizaban helicópteros, filmaban arrestos y se jactaban de ellos en las redes sociales.</p><p>Aún así, muchos de los arrestos recientes han ocurrido en espacios públicos, como cortes, escuelas y supermercados.</p><p>La vasta mayoría de los recientes detenidos en Chicago también no tienen antecedentes penales, dijo Berto Aguayo, abogado y copresidente de políticas del Consejo de Liderazgo Latino.</p><p>“A pesar de las afirmaciones de que el 'Operativo Midway Blitz' ha terminado, no es así”, dijo Aguayo. “Nuestras comunidades continúan sintiendo el impacto. Las familias siguen viviendo con las consecuencias y la litigación continúa hasta el día de hoy debido al daño continuo causado por este operativo”.</p><p>“Así que nuestro mensaje hoy sigue siendo el mismo: Si eres vulnerable, por favor toma precauciones y limita salir; conoce tus derechos, mantente informado; conéctate con organizaciones comunitarias de confianza y tus vecinos”.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-1d517b" name="image-1d517b"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/c8d4ad2/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1024x575+0+54/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Ff9%2Fb3%2F2a2c49724a32a05f36f63e3e7399%2Fice-260710-5.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/7b8d295/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1024x575+0+54/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Ff9%2Fb3%2F2a2c49724a32a05f36f63e3e7399%2Fice-260710-5.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/20b03f4/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1024x575+0+54/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Ff9%2Fb3%2F2a2c49724a32a05f36f63e3e7399%2Fice-260710-5.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Berto Aguayo, copresidente del Consejo de Liderazgo Latino, habla con periodistas durante una conferencia de prensa el jueves para denunciar un aumento de la actividad de ICE en la zona. La conferencia se realizó en la intersección de 47th Street y Damen Avenue, en el barrio de Back of the Yards.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Tyler Pasciak LaRiviere/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>La operación menos ostentosa de ICE ha afectado a los residentes “de una buena y de una mala manera”, dijo Rodríguez.</p><p>“De una buena manera porque hay cierto alivio que se siente de alguna manera para algunas personas”, detalló Rodríguez. “Pero de una mala manera porque… me preocuparía que nos sintamos cómodos con el silencio, aunque en realidad no está realmente silencioso, simplemente no es tan visible como solía ser. Así que eso pone a las personas en peligro”.</p><p>En el último mes, el número de solicitudes de servicios legales de inmigración realizadas al Proyecto Resurrección ha aumentado casi el doble, de 900 consultas a más de 1,700, dijo el director ejecutivo de la organización, Raul Raymundo.</p><p>Otros grupos han visto el mismo aumento en las consultas.</p><p>En Enlace Chicago, las solicitudes de servicios han aumentado significativamente en las últimas semanas, aseguró Rodríguez.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure entries.title: Chicago murals: Albany Park artist draws inspiration from science

Avenue, she called experts at the Shedd Aquarium for insight on native Lake Michigan flora and fauna, and invasive critters, too.</p><p>The result is a massive spread in <a class="Link" Invasive sea lamprey adhere to the purple columns in the murals.</p><p>While realistic, Robbins also “wanted the piece to remain optimistic.” Colorful images that look like rainbow trees were inspired by viewing butterfly wings under a microscope, she says, and the lights of fireflies seem to flash underneath.</p><p>“That’s my main goal that I want viewers to take away from the artwork,” Robbins says. “I want them to be excited about learning about all these flora and fauna that make up this environment.”</p><p>Her murals represent second chances in a way, too. entries.title: White Sox activate Munetaka Murakami from injured list, option Jacob Gonzalez to Charlotte
entries.summary: <p>The White Sox officially activated Munetaka Murakami from the injured list Friday and optioned Jacob Gonzalez to Triple-A Charlotte. </p><p>Murakami, who played in two rehab games this week in Charlotte to complete his recovery from a strained right hamstring, will be in the lineup for the game tonight against the Athletics at Rate Field (6:40 p.m., CHSN, 1000-AM). A sellout crowd is expected.</p><p>“He feels good. He’s ready to go,” manager Will Venable said Thursday when he announced that Murakami would be activated after a successful rehab assignment. “He was challenged running the bases. Defensively, had a really long game yesterday of nine innings. So [we] feel good about the work; he recovered well today. So he’s ready to go.”</p><p>Murakami, who still ranks second on the team with 20 home runs, went 2-for-7 with an RBI double, a walk and two strikeouts at Charlotte. He played five innings at first base Tuesday and nine innings Wednesday. The Sox might give Murakami some time at designated hitter as he returns to game-playing shape.</p><p>“There’ll be a lot of communication on where he’s at,” Venable said. “This ramp-up and this rehab was obviously very quick. So we want to be mindful of where he’s at day to day.”</p><p>Murakami, 26, has missed the last 35 games, in which the Sox held their own with a record of 17-18. Before suffering the injury running to first base May 30, Murakami was slashing .240/.378/.560 with four doubles, 41 RBI, 44 walks and 43 runs scored in 57 games. His 20 homers are tied for seventh in the American League.</p><p>The Sox called up Gonzalez, 24, the day after Murakami's injury — which he suffered six weeks ago today — and put him through a crash course at first base. After some early mental mistakes, Gonzalez caught on and capably handled the position. He had hoped that his ability to play everywhere else on the infield — he has been a shortstop for most of his career — would keep him with the Sox when Murakami returned.</p><p>“We all know I can play all the positions,” he told the Sun-Times on Thursday. “Obviously, I came up here to fill the first-baseman role while he was hurt. I think it was good I showed that I can play there." </p><p>Gonzalez slashed .244/.323/.360 with four doubles, two home runs, 17 RBI and 11 runs scored in 30 games with the Sox in his first major-league season.</p><p>Murakami is returning at a time the Sox' offense is sputtering. In losing all three games to the Red Sox this week, the White Sox scored two runs with 15 hits — all singles — in 27 innings and struck out 25 times.</p><p>“Obviously, he’s a presence in the lineup,” designated hitter Andrew Benintendi said. “He’ll bring energy. Seems like the vibe in here is kind of down right now. But I’m sure seeing him will spark it back up.”</p><p>“It’s going to be a great jolt,” Venable said. “That’s real. We understand the impact that he makes on the field and in the clubhouse. Really excited about it.”</p><div class="PageListL" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" data-show-loadmore="true" ><a class="AnchorLink"
